claims.claim: a couple of hundred AWS keys taken in a few windows in late October, including from requests rejected before any model ran

claims.claim: a privacy flag only binds the first hop; routers/resellers inherit downstream logging

claims.claim: Affected: three AI providers, not named in the post
claims.quote: Searched whole post: breached providers are not named; SurplusIntelligence, OpenRouter, Anthropic appear only in a Figure 7 caption, ARTEX is the attacker tool

claims.claim: Fixed in / Severity: not stated in the post
claims.quote: Searched whole post: no severity rating. Fix status: Dragos is working with 'about a dozen providers'; 'One provider has published a preliminary security notice'; another 'has still not publicly disclosed the incident'
claims.fix: Severity is indeed not stated. 'Fixed in' is not a version question but the post does give remediation status: one provider has published a preliminary security notice, another has not disclosed, and stolen keys/URLs were still being accessed months later. Say that instead of 'not stated'.

claims.claim: Stopgap: go direct to first-tier provider, choose upstream providers yourself, avoid reseller marketplaces, enable secret filtering
claims.quote: 'Use a first-tier provider'; 'Choose upstream providers yourself, verify that privacy settings change request routing, and avoid reseller marketplaces'; secret filtering 'not a panacea'; also self-host ('only option where no one else reads your prompts')
claims.fix: Also add: self-host if hardware allows, add user agents artex-agent and artex-judge-r121 to detections, and note secret filtering is 'not a panacea'.

claims.claim: If compromised: not stated in the post as a procedure
claims.quote: Searched whole post: no credential-rotation or incident-response procedure; only 'Seed your own canaries' and 'treat any use as an incident'
